Global tensions have escalated with Ukraine launching drone attacks on Russia, prompting a response that raises concerns about prolonged conflict. On another front, the Strait of Hormuz oil flow has returned to pre-war levels. All these developments indicate shifts in leverage and positioning among regional actors. On a more optimistic note, scientists have made significant breakthroughs in two crucial areas: hydrogen production and AI computing efficiency. We've just witnessed a major lab mistake that might revolutionize computing by significantly reducing the energy consumption of AI processes. This achievement is part and parcel with our understanding of how data processing consumes vast amounts of power. In terms of grid resilience, we're witnessing a seismic shift in the global energy landscape. Over the past four years, 20 nuclear reactors worth of battery storage have been added to the US grid, exemplifying rapid deployment of large-scale battery storage and integration of renewable energy sources. This momentum underscores the critical role of grid resilience, as it's essential to absorb physical or political shocks. As for speculative possibilities in the Final Frontier, we're seeing significant developments. Amazon has launched its Kuiper satellite constellation from Florida, directly challenging SpaceX's Starlink dominance. Additionally, California is introducing new electric vehicle incentives and Tesla will begin deploying airbags on these vehicles.
